newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediobanca net interest income down in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Mediobanca net interest income down in Q1.

text.p: Italian investment bank Mediobanca posted parent net interest income in the first quarter ended September 30 of 192 billion lire, 87 billion lire down on the same year-ago period, managing director Vincenzo Maranghi said.
He told a shareholders meeting the fall was due to loan interest rates coming down at a faster pace than interest rates payable on deposits.

Loans and credit advances as at September 30 against June 30 were down 1.08 trillion lire, "a fall of five to six percent," Maranghi said. In the first quarter of the year-ago period they fell by 257 billion lire, down 1.4 percent.
Total deposits at September 30 rose by 455 billion lire from end-June. In the first year-ago quarter they were up 41 billion lire. No details of current totals were given.
Net assets at end-September totalled 6.50 trillion lire, or 13,645 lire per share.

Mediobanca's investment portfolio, value October 25, equalled 3.63 trillion lire, up 66 billion from end-June. Maranghi said at current values, the bank had a theoretical net capital gain of 1.563 trillion lire compared with 2.165 trillion lire at end-June.
